Our LPDDR5 subsystem is causing periodic stalls during dynamic frequency scaling. When the memory controller attempts to transition from 3200MHz to 1600MHz to save power, the self-refresh exit latency exceeds the programmed timeout and the DFS operation stalls for 50-80ms, causing visible UI jank.

ftrace output:
  kworker/0:1-42  [000] 500.100: devfreq_frequency: dev=soc:memory-controller freq=3200000000
  kworker/0:1-42  [000] 500.101: ddr_sr_entry: latency=1200ns
  kworker/0:1-42  [000] 500.102: devfreq_set_freq: target=1600000000
  kworker/0:1-42  [000] 500.103: ddr_sr_exit: START
  kworker/0:1-42  [000] 500.155: ddr_sr_exit: COMPLETE latency=52400000ns  <-- 52.4ms!
  kworker/0:1-42  [000] 500.156: devfreq_frequency: dev=soc:memory-controller freq=1600000000

LPDDR5 MR readback:
  MR4[2:0] = 0x5 (temperature > 85C)
  MR19 (DQS interval timer): 0x04
  MR28 (training pattern): unchanged

The stall only happens when the DRAM temperature is high. At room temp the transition takes <1ms. What's going on?
